overall: The AG found one email from the Chairman to a fellow commissioner (Nov 18, 2018) was an unlawful deliberation; the other complaints were untimely or unsupported and were dismissed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a quorum deliberated by email (Nov 16-19, 2018 exchange about rescheduling the Sewer Project discussion) outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Complainant was aware of these emails on November 16, 17, and 19, 2018, her December 26, 2018, complaint alleging that the emails constituted improper deliberation outside of a posted meeting is untimely.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Chairman's Nov 18, 2018 one-line email to Commissioner Murphy, sent to a quorum-forming member, was deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that Chairman Searle’s November 18 email to Commissioner Murphy expressing his agreement with Commissioner Murphy’s earlier emailed opinions was not merely about scheduling, but rather was an expression of agreement with Commissioner Murphy’s opinions regarding the Complainant’s harassing behavior and lack of courtesy.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged generally that a quorum deliberated outside posted meetings through emails about Sewer Project directives and actions (Oct-Nov 2018).
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find the December 28 complaint was not timely filed, and we decline to review the allegations raised.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission did not fully respond to a public records request, and argued this showed unposted deliberation; the AG treated it only as evidence in the deliberation claim.
allegations.key_passage: We do not find that these additional communications constitute deliberation, but rather relate to the scheduling of meetings and similar administrative tasks that the Open Meeting Law excludes from the definition of “deliberation.”

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission agreed on Amended Sewer Decision changes outside its March 12, 2019 noticed meeting, voting on it immediately without discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we decline to find that the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside of a noticed meeting.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that similar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
